purpose: Track the strength of evidence behind high-use misconception records separately from diagnostic route coverage. A concept may have a usable diagnostic route while the exact misconception wording remains curriculum-inferred or research-required.

status_definitions.direct_empirical: A checked original study directly supports the relevant reasoning pattern within stated sample limits.
status_definitions.direct_empirical_broad_construct_or_mech: An original study supports the broader construct or cognitive mechanism, but not every detail of the MathBridge wording or target age range.
status_definitions.evidence_synthesis: An evidence-reviewed practice guide or research synthesis supports the instructional interpretation.
status_definitions.guidance_supported: Official teaching guidance supports the instructional risk or response, but direct misconception-specific empirical evidence has not been checked.
status_definitions.curriculum_inferred: The reasoning pattern is plausible from the mathematical structure/curriculum but direct evidence for the exact claim is not yet verified.
status_definitions.research_required: The exact wording is stronger than the evidence currently verified and should not be presented as research-established.

publication_rules: Never convert direct evidence from one population into a jurisdictional prevalence claim.
A diagnostic item remains an instructional probe unless independently validated as an assessment instrument.
If evidence supports only a broader construct, teacher-facing text must use possible/may language rather than state a fixed misconception.
Evidence depth does not alter curriculum placement evidence.
